events.title: Spot P! Opening Reception
events.location: Dyckman Farmhouse Museum (in Dyckman House Museum)
events.description: Come and celebrate the opening of Spot P! by Kasper Klop, Deron Gopie, and Morwenna Spagnol. Free and open to the public, but registration is required.Monuments are symbols of an acknowledged history, of a collective thinking… What world do we live in if laws have abolished slavery and monuments reflect it? Why does the law not apply to legacy in our society and our community?Peter Stuyvesant is often credited with laying the foundations for what became New York City. Today, this man of Dutch origin is celebrated all around town: statues, neighborhoods in his name, cigarette brand…Yet, if we take a closer look, he was a trader and owner of enslaved Africans in the United States. Bolstered by his fortune and his influence, he sold enslaved people at public auction, held and expressed deeply antisemitic views, violently oppressed the Lenape, and actively suppressed religious minorities.Dutch artist Kasper Klop asked himself: what is my responsibility to reckon with this history as a Dutch person, and what would happen if the full story got told, rather than a partial one, as so often happens in our commemorative landscape?In collaboration with his long-time artistic partner Morwenna Spagnol, and videographer Deron Gopie, Kasper and the team created a multiple choice survey investigating how much New Yorkers really know about Stuyvesant, and once they know the facts, what they think about them.Spot P! at Dyckman Farmhouse Museum showcases New Yorkers’ fascinating replies to the survey, their knowledge (or lack thereof), views, astonishment, powerlessness, indifference, outrage and nuanced responses that grappled with holding multiple contradictions at once. Also on view are extracts from primary source materials – that is, what Stuyvesant wrote in his own hand about his dark deeds, along with insights into how the team intercepted busy pedestrians (including quite a few rejections), and obtained video consent forms for all the final material on display today.Spot P! will be on view at Dyckman Farmhouse Museum from October 29, 2026 to January 30, 2027.This program is supported by The Holland Society of New York and DutchCultureUSA, a program of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in the United States.

events.title: Pumpkin Smash
events.location: La Plaza Cultural
events.description: Bring your pumpkins, gourds, and jack-o'-lanterns to LES Ecology Center's PUMPKIN SMASH! You smash them, and we'll turn them into compost! Enjoy fun family-friendly activities and light refreshments! ACTIVITIES 12pm - 3pm (ongoing):Pumpkin Smash Zone: Weigh and record your pumpkins, then choose your smashing tool! Toss your pumpkin to crack it open, or give it a good whack with a bat or mallet. Finish the job with an ice chopper to break it into smaller pieces, which helps it compost faster. Painting with Food Scraps: Get creative with our watercolor paints, created from food scraps and plant materials. Experiment with different colors and watch how they change as they dry! Typewriter Poetry with Climate Cafe NYC: Join Jayshawn Lee from the Climate Imaginarium for personalized poems. We encourage you to paint on your poem for an extra special keepsake. 1:30pm - 2:30pm Community Drumming Circle: Please join us for a community drumming circle, with guidance from Fabio Puentes. Drums will be provided, and since supplies are limited, we’ll take turns so everyone gets a chance to play! FREE and open to all ages! Registration is recommended here, but drop-ins are always welcome. Light rain or shine. Inclement weather date: Sun. 11/15. We'll post updates on social media and our website.

events.title: Second Sunday Castle Tours
events.location: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)
events.description: The Bayside Historical Society's staff and volunteers are offering guided tours of The Castle and its exhibitions on the second Sunday of each month from 1pm-3pm. Each tour lasts approximately 45 minutes; two tours are offered, with the first beginning at 1:00 PM and the second at 2:00 PM. Admission is free, but reservations are required. Reserve your spot in advance for the November 8th tour by booking your free tickets at www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/second-sunday-castle-tours-27.The Castle in Fort Totten is one of New York City's finest surviving examples of Gothic Revival castellated-style architecture. Completed in 1887, the building originally served as the Officers' Mess Hall and Club for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers School of Application. Come explore this architectural treasure in Bayside and learn more about its fascinating history.

events.description: GreenThumb community gardens are developed, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces.Clara's Garden is a quiet green oasis in East New York that is seeking volunteers to help build new garden beds and plant natives! Join us for a hands-on volunteer day! No prior experience necessary - beginners are welcome! Come learn about the neighborhood's community gardens. GreenThumb will provide supplies and facilitation.This is a great opportunity to support a dynamic community space while learning about urban agriculture. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note: Some tasks may involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here! Location: 579 Glenmore Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11207For information about group volunteering, please contact Volunteer Program Coordinator, Olivia Navarro at Olivia.Navarro@parks.nyc.govThis event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: Harlem Run: Monday Night Run
events.location: Marcus Garvey Park
events.description: Harlem Run brings free weekly and inclusive pacer-led runs and walks throughout Harlem. Join us for a different route through Harlem, beginning and ending at Marcus Garvey Park. Paces available include 7 min to 12 min, run/walk, and walk groups. Open to all ages and abilities. Bag drop available, though not guaranteed.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: Forest Fitness
events.location: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)
events.description: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. All classes end with closing with stretches.(Note: Fitness Walking does not meet if it is raining or if the actual temperature or wind chill is below 20 degrees F.)
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: Garden Conflict Transformation Circle— A 2-Month Journey for Community Gardeners | Session #2
events.location: Virtual/Online Workshop
events.description: Even the most harmonious garden groups experience conflict—it's as natural as weeds sprouting between the tomatoes. But what if those challenging moments could become opportunities for deeper connection and stronger communities? Join mediators Skye Roper-Moses and Michelle Jackson for an intimate, two-month learning cohort designed specifically for community gardeners who are ready to transform the way they navigate conflict.Session 1: Conflict Transformation CircleShare real-life challenges in a confidential, supportive space with fellow gardeners. Together, you’ll co-create solutions and learn practical skills you can take directly back to your garden.Session 2: Conflict Transformation Experiential LabDeepen your practice through hands-on exercises. Learn how to address tensions before they take root and gain confidence facilitating difficult conversations.Whether you’re facing personality clashes over plot boundaries or navigating group dynamics, this cohort will give you the tools to turn conflict into fertile ground for growth. Come ready to dig deep—transform challenges into connections. Register Here NYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: NYRR Open Run: Brooklyn Bridge Park
events.location: Pier 6 (in Brooklyn Bridge Park)
events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, weekly community-led, approximately 3 mile runs to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.The Open Run route offers views of the Brooklyn Bridge on the way out, the Statue of Liberty on the way back, and the Lower Manhattan skyline the whole way. Fornino is a great spot to get drinks and pizza after the run.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.
